familyMembers.bio: Thomas inherited his father's craftsmanship and ran Hawthorne Architectural Woodworking for 35 years. Passionate about sailing, vintage cars, and family genealogies.

familyMembers.bio: Botanist and high school biology educator. Marianne cultivates an award-winning heirloom rose garden and coordinates the annual coastal family picnic.

familyMembers.bio: Historian, archivist, and creator of the Hawthorne Digital Heritage Archive. Clara digitizes family negatives, letters, and recipes to keep memories vibrant across generations.

familyMembers.favoriteMemory: Listening to Grandpa Artie recount his sea voyages by the crackling hearth.

familyMembers.bio: Architectural photographer and avid cyclist. Documentarian of family reunions and holidays.

memories.title: Nana Ellie's Secret Cardamom Spiced Apple Cake
memories.author: Eleanor Hawthorne (Transcribed by Clara)
memories.content: This recipe was taught to Eleanor by her Irish grandmother, with a dash of cardamom introduced after moving to Boston. The secret is grating half the apples fine for moisture and chunking the other half for texture.
recipeIngredients: 3 large farm eggs at room temperature
1 cup organic unsalted sweet cream butter (melted & cooled)
4 crisp Cortland or Honeycrisp apples (2 finely grated, 2 peeled & cubed)
recipeSteps: Preheat the woodstove oven (or modern oven) to 350°F (175°C). Butter and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan thoroughly.
In a large stoneware bowl, whisk together the flour, cinnamon, cardamom, baking soda, and salt until fragrant.
In another bowl, beat brown sugar and melted butter, then whisk in eggs one at a time until glossy.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry mixture until just combined (do not overwork the batter).
Gently fold in the grated apples, diced apples, walnuts, and vanilla extract.
Pour into prepared pan and bake for 55 to 65 minutes until a wooden skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 20 minutes before turning out onto an heirloom ceramic plate. Dust with confectioners' sugar.
